objective: Find course creators and educators who need to turn a rights-cleared lecture archive into trustworthy notes, translations, books, or cited search without losing its source trail.

lazyblog.need: Help a lecture-first learner turn the opening ideas of state, evolution, reversibility, phase space, and vectors into derivations and exercises they can reproduce.
lazyblog.policy: The article is a complete educational answer first. The archive appears only as a quiet study aid after the official lecture and independent exercises; no service, donation, hardware, or unrelated portfolio pitch was added.

x.content: Own a lecture archive? Keep timestamps, speaker turns, slide references, corrections and source rights before turning it into a book. That provenance layer makes notes, translation and search easier to trust. One example: https://github.com/lachlanchen/leonardsusskind

x.policy: A useful first-party note about preserving provenance. The linked repository is a maintained format example, not customer proof or an offer to resell lecture content.

reddit.policy: Reply only when a current course or archive owner asks how to preserve or repurpose material they control. Solve the question in the reply; link only where the community permits it.

instagram.policy: Do not make a generic graphic. Show a real project-owned or openly licensed source-to-study transformation if one becomes available.

hackernews.policy: Use current archive and course-production questions for research only; do not post agent-authored comments.

limits: Use only customer-owned, public-domain, or clearly licensed recordings, slides, transcripts, translations, and images.
The Susskind archive demonstrates a maintained study format; it is not a customer result or content offered for resale.
Do not promise automated accuracy, publication, hosting, or delivery terms before a bounded sample is reviewed.
